problem: Let $F(x)={x}^{2}-2x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **even** extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ What is $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,0)?$

feedback.worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [0,\pi ),$ the even extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}F(x), & x\in [0,\pi ), \\ F(-x), & x\in (-\pi ,0).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, for $x\in (-\pi ,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =F(-x) \\  & =(2(-x)+1){e}^{2(-x)} \\  & =(-2x+1){e}^{-2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) & =(-2(-2)+1){e}^{-2(-2)}=5{e}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
